at_sea:
NOTHING IN FLIGHT. sail:the-heartbeat-outlives-its-caller reached PROVED at 17:05 on 2026-08-18 and both repos are clean and pushed (cairn d1a125f, commons f373df6).

WHAT WAS BUILT. superclaude spawned the ground loop with setsid, which detaches a tty and does nothing to a cgroup, so the loop lived in the session's own scope and died with the window — measured, not suspected: one cgroup string for both loop and caller, beats frozen at 1 across the kill. It is a transient user unit now (systemd-run --user), so the manager owns it. Three costs, all in launchers/intention+why.json: SuccessExitStatus=3 (the singleton loser exits 3 BY DESIGN, and a nonzero exit leaves a transient unit loaded in `failed` holding its own name); --setenv=HOME and --setenv=PATH (systemd-run hands the unit the MANAGER's environment, and a PATH without ~/.cairn/venv/bin is a loop that cannot import itself); and a HELD NAME never falls through to setsid, because that would be a second claimant racing the first. Only an UNREACHABLE systemd is a legitimate fall-through.

THE PREDICATE WORTH CARRYING ELSEWHERE: a '.scope' is a cgroup built AROUND processes someone else forked (lifetime = the forker's); a '.service' is one the manager forked and owns. Green is service, red is scope. The chart raised 'what counts as a terminal?' as an open unknown and it DISSOLVED — konsole, tmux, sshd and whatever ships next all fall out without being named.

RESHAPED MID-BUILD BY ITS OWN COST MEASUREMENT. The falsifier lists DELAY as wrong intent, so three round trips to the manager became one: the liveness probe is gone because THE START ATTEMPT IS THE PROBE (stricter, not just cheaper — the old shape committed to systemd the moment its proxy passed), and reset-failed moved to the retry. Cost n=15, interleaved arms: setsid 76.1ms median, unit 118.0ms. ~42ms, recorded with NO gate — one reading is not a threshold.

EVIDENCE: red first (5 of 24 arms, unmodified tree at 124442b), green four times, sealed twice under the tester in netns. Live loop 574986 is launcher-started and beating.

ALSO CAST, and it is the only thing owed forward: the-memory-curve-is-recorded-not-eyeballed.

open_threads:
1. THE WATCH IS NOT SATISFIED, and this is the most important line here. WATCHME(the_heartbeat_outlives_its_caller) crossed and the probe is armed at cairn/devices/ground_loop/probes/does_the_heartbeat_outlive_its_caller.py — but the live fire used a stand-in binary that exits immediately, so outlived_its_spawner came back True against a 70-second-old loop. That was the FIXTURE meeting `enough`, not a caller dying. The ticket ruled on this in advance. What the watch waits for is a real session's death. DO NOT read a green probe as the watch clearing until a real session has ended under it.

2. CONSTRAIN FLOOR IS BLIND TO THREE RUNGS — a real defect, no ticket yet. charter_constraints comes back [] for every ref under launchers/, bin/ and skills/, because address.component_of is rooted at <repo>/cairn. The bounds for this voyage were read by hand from charters the floor should have surfaced. Owed: a ticket.

3. THE HARBOR'S CLEARANCE GATE WAS ABSENT FROM THE WHOLE CHART CHAIN. Nothing in orient, survey or validate knew a forward crossing into a REST needs harbor_master.clearance.clear, nor that it needs a machine-readable gated_by on the component's charter. Both were discovered by being refused at the door. launchers now declares gated_by ['Akien','CC'] — a translation of its existing prose owner, NOT a new grant. Worth checking which other beside-code charters still lack it before their first REST crossing.

4. FOUR CHART INSTRUMENTS WERE WRONG and are named in the ticket's chart_feedback: criterion 1 specified a killpg where only a cgroup kill can prove its own claim (setsid has already left the process group, so a killpg would have gone green on the BROKEN launcher); criterion 6 assumed the probe's __main__ took a pid when it silently ignored one; criterion 7's grep cannot tell a mention from a read (10 hits, 1 reader); decompose's writes_to needed correcting.

5. THE SCORE: 225 tool calls between the validate berth and done, read downward. It honestly contains a mid-build redesign, a timing harness built and run three times, and two gate refusals — a thin packet and a hard build give the same number, which is the metric's limit.

6. deletegate REFUSES ANY rm WHOSE COMMAND CONTAINS THE SUBSTRING '.cairn', including scratchpad paths that merely mention it. Hit twice this voyage. The door is bin/cmd/trash. No ticket.

7. RETRACTED THIS SESSION: I reported the live loop at ~16 s/beat and called it worse than the 7-14x a-beat-costs-what-changed was cast on. That was measured while 14 loops MY OWN cost harness had leaked held the box at load average 18.7. Re-measured quiet: 8.57 s/beat windowed, 9.11 lifetime — inside the cast range. Appended to that ticket rather than dropped.

8. STILL STANDING, untouched: the 15x ground-loop-is-older-than-the-code-it-judges trouble is factually stale, but clearing it is the recipient's act through the lane's door, not mine.
